reading:
Element Critical is a privately held colocation operator backed by Mercuria, 26North, Arctos, and Safanad, per Mercuria's own press release announcing the platform's launch, though this entry could not fetch the release's full text due to a certificate error and relies on its title and search snippet. The operator's own About page did not state a headquarters address, founding year, or a single clear corporate home city among its three named markets, so headquarters is left unrecorded here.

The company names three locations, Austin, Houston, and Chicago, and describes support for scalable deployments up to 50 megawatts, positioning itself around power-dense AI and GPU infrastructure and ultra-high density colocation. Trade press from Data Center Dynamics and Data Center Frontier separately reports Element Critical acquiring two data centers in the Chicago suburbs. Its named target industries span emerging technology, cloud and network service providers, gaming, higher education, healthcare, and financial services.

The registry here tracks 2 Element Critical facilities, both in Illinois, consistent with the Chicago-area acquisition reported in trade press. Element Critical's stated 50 megawatt deployment ceiling and AI/GPU positioning place it among the smaller AI-focused colocation operators in this registry, distinct in scale from the multi-hundred-megawatt campuses recorded for NTT, CloudHQ, and Vantage.
